clue.text: Come to pass, perhaps, in the Yorkshire dales?

definitions.meaning: to come to pass is to occur or take place
in Yorkshire dialect the word for 'occur' is also used to mean maybe or perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether something might take place out in the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition relies on northern English dialect, where people say 'happen it'll rain' for 'perhaps it will rain'; the Yorkshire Dales are hill country in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: one means to occur, the other is a Yorkshire dialect adverb meaning maybe.

clue.text: Agent losing female player

indicators.note: losing means the agent word drops a letter

parts.note: an agent or contributing cause is a factor

explanation.surface: An agent drops a female performer from the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' suggests a theatrical agent, but it is a factor, a cause; losing F leaves the performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer is a player.

clue.text: Don't make jokes cruelly or bitterly

definitions.meaning: advice to make your wordplay jokes kindly rather than harshly
sharply or acridly, as of a smell or remark

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic instruction: make puns, but softly. Split the answer as PUN GENTLY to see it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes a sharp, biting smell or a caustic remark; split in two it is an instruction to joke kindly.

clue.text: Form of pasta — not the sensible kind

definitions.meaning: informally, a silly person, a fool

explanation.definitionFit: It is a strip of pasta, and informally a foolish person.

clue.text: Trio sang this musician's composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters of the preceding words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A trio has sung a piece written by a particular musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks like the musical work the trio sang, but it signals rearranging the letters of TRIO SANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A church or concert keyboard player of the pipe instrument is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Writer, as it happens, runs into old metal-worker

indicators.note: the runs piece goes into the old metal-worker, so one is placed inside the other

parts.note: a goldsmith works precious metal
live describes something broadcast as it happens
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An author, by chance, bumps into a craftsman of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' looks like a filler phrase, but it describes a live broadcast; 'into' sends that and the runs inside the old metal-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish-born author of The Vicar of Wakefield and She Stoops to Conquer.

clue.text: Liberal urges one amendment

indicators.note: an amendment is an alteration, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician presses for a change to a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The political Liberal and the amendment are decoys: 'amendment' rearranges URGES ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of open-handed and giving freely.

clue.text: Desert area in Nevada, say

indicators.note: the word for 'say' goes in the state abbreviation

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A desert region found in Nevada, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevada has deserts, which suggests an American one, but the desert is in southern Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the large arid region of southern Israel.

clue.text: City featured as almanac has articles rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged plainly says the letters of the fodder words are put in another order

explanation.surface: A city appears in an almanac whose articles have been reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' works on AS ALMANAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamanca is a historic university city in western Spain.

clue.text: Motley collection of tenors aint making much noise

indicators.note: a motley collection is a jumbled assortment, so the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: A ragtag group of tenors is anything but quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motley collection of' rearranges the letters of TENORS AINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian describes a voice that is extremely loud and powerful, after Stentor, the loud-voiced herald in Homer.

clue.text: Security for Napoleon's little daughter

definitions.meaning: a ...-edged government bond, a safe investment
Napoleon is the boar in Orwell's Animal Farm, so his young daughter would be a young female pig

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a safe investment to provide for the Emperor Napoleon's young daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The emperor is a decoy: the Napoleon meant is the pig who rules Orwell's Animal Farm, and a young sow is called a gilt. A gilt is also a British government bond.
explanation.definitionFit: In finance a gilt is a safe UK government bond; in farming the word names a young female pig that has not yet farrowed.

clue.text: Genuine sportsman of the right sort

parts.note: genuine means true
a blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University at sport

explanation.surface: An authentic athlete who is a thoroughly decent type.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman awarded colours; blue is also the colour of the Conservative Party, hence 'the right' in the political sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means staunchly loyal, especially a dyed-in-the-wool Conservative, a member of the political right.

clue.text: Engineers given siren to patch up

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
a siren is a seductive woman, a vamp

explanation.surface: Engineers are told to mend a warning siren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'siren' suggests a warning horn the engineers repair, but here it is a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp is to renovate or fix up something old.

clue.text: Second prize for competitor at Crufts?

parts.note: a pot is a trophy or prize, as in a sports cup

explanation.surface: A runner-up's award given to an entrant at a dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show; the question mark signals the definition by example, a typical dog's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic pet dog's name, so a dog entered in a show might be called this.

clue.text: Picture a small group employed for light detective work

parts.note: a photo is a picture
a cell is a small group, as of activists

explanation.surface: A photograph of a little gang hired to do some undemanding sleuthing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light detective work' sounds like minor sleuthing; it means detecting light.
explanation.definitionFit: A photoelectric cell is a device that senses light and responds electrically.

clue.text: Chap tucking into fruit is a glutton

indicators.note: the chap is tucked inside the fruit, one word placed within another

parts.note: a gourd is a hard-shelled fruit
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man greedily eating fruit is a greedy eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' reads as the glutton eating, which fits the surface, but it is a container signal: the chap goes inside the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a person who eats to excess, a greedy eater.

clue.text: Moving review that made Browning yearn for home

definitions.meaning: a parade of troops passing a saluting point

definitions.text: that made Browning yearn for home
definitions.meaning: in Home-Thoughts, from Abroad, Robert Browning longs to be in England now that April has arrived

explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem opens 'Oh, to be in England / Now that April's there', so the end of the preceding month set off his homesickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial military parade, and literally the month before April having gone by.

clue.text: Victory, for example, for a soldier

definitions.meaning: HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship, is a fighting warship

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an armed sailing warship like HMS Victory, and also a warrior.

clue.text: Locks secured, in the end, with £25 left

indicators.note: left says the money piece sits on the left of the other piece

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
the tail is the end part of something

explanation.surface: Hair tied back with the remaining twenty-five pounds spent at the hairdresser.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for £25, and 'left' places it before TAIL, the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This hairstyle is hair gathered and tied at the back of the head, so the locks are fastened.

clue.text: Horse galloped round the ring

indicators.note: the run goes round the ring, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: galloped means ran
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A horse raced around the circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts RAN around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat has white hairs mixed with another colour.

clue.text: Rugby forward, this chap

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union
forward means cheeky or pert

explanation.surface: A rugby forward, this fellow here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a rugby position but means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so it can stand for some particular chap.

clue.text: Jeers a blunder

definitions.meaning: repeated shouts of derision from a crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Two booing jeers in a row; and as one word, informal slang for an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Show correctness as French force overcomes Italian

indicators.note: in a down entry, overcomes puts the force piece above the Italian piece

parts.note: the BEF, British Expeditionary Force, was sent to France

explanation.surface: French troops defeat an Italian army, which seems only proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French force' is not a French army: it is the British Expeditionary Force, which served in France in both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fitting or appropriate, to suit, as good manners suit an occasion.

clue.text: Bridge player encounters hand depending on unorthodox lead

parts.note: in bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West
a paw is a hand, informally

explanation.surface: A card player meets a hand that relies on an unconventional opening card.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting suggests leading a card, but the lead is a boxer's leading fist: a left-hander leads with the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed boxer stands with the right fist forward, the reverse of the orthodox stance.

clue.text: Set up a time and a place for contest

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the time word is read upwards

parts.note: an era is a time
'n is short for and

explanation.surface: Fix a date and a venue for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns ERA into ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sport or combat.

clue.text: Worker with fine physique

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A labourer with a good build.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, brawn or muscle is beef, a strong body.

clue.text: Government policy statement not used by FT

definitions.meaning: a UK government document setting out proposed legislation
the Financial Times is printed on pink newsprint, so it avoids the usual colourless sheets

explanation.definitionFit: It names a government report on future policy, and literally the plain pale sheets the pink Financial Times does without.

clue.text: Some money in deposit required by shrewd biographer

indicators.note: the money goes in the deposit, placed inside it

parts.note: to deposit is to put down
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra
arch means knowing or cunning

explanation.surface: A canny writer of lives needs some cash put down as a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside PUT; 'required by' simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was the Greek author of the Parallel Lives of famous Greeks and Romans.

clue.text: Old master shows giant holding one

indicators.note: the giant holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a titan is a giant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Old Master's painting depicts a giant clutching something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside TITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance painter is one of the great European painters before 1800.
